subject: Clarification: streaming vs batch SLA for Acme POC
messages:
From: Ethan Moore <ethan.moore@acme.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Streaming vs batch SLA — need specifics for POC

Sean —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our production team is evaluating Redwood for a latency-sensitive feature that streams real-time suggestions into our editor. Before we sign the POC statement of work we need two things clarified in writing:

1) For streaming endpoints, what are your measurable SLA commitments for time-to-first-token (TTFT) and sustained token/sec? We need p95 numbers and guidance for short (<=128 tokens) and long (>=1024 tokens) responses.
2) How does that differ from your non-streaming (batch or blocking) endpoints in both TTFT and tokens/sec?

We also have a constraint: the editor needs a TTFT of <=350ms p95 and a sustained 800-1200 tokens/sec for the typical workload. If Redwood can only guarantee that on Dedicated, that’s fine — we just need an exception written into the POC acceptance criteria.

Can you send a short doc or a formal exception we can include in the SOW?

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Moore
ENG Manager, Real-Time Systems
Acme Corp

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Moore <ethan.moore@acme.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming vs batch SLA — need specifics for POC

Ethan —

Appreciate the clear ask. I pulled Karthik and Marissa in so we can give concrete numbers and an explicit exception for the POC. High level answer: streaming guarantees are different vs non-streaming and are typically delivered from Dedicated capacity. I've attached a short draft SLA and our recent runtime latency report for reference.

Summary (quick bullets):
- Hosted (shared) plan: Best-effort streaming TTFT; no formal p95 for streaming on shared. Uptime SLA: 99.9%.
- Dedicated: We can commit to a TTFT p95 <= 350 ms for streaming endpoints for short outputs (<=128 tokens) and <= 450 ms p95 for long outputs (>=1024 tokens), assuming the model and instance class in the SOW.
- Sustained token throughput (Dedicated): baseline guarantee 1,200 tokens/sec sustained per provisioned serving lane (p95). Burst capacity available up to ~2,500 tokens/sec for short intervals.
- Non-streaming (blocking) endpoints: we define latency as time-to-complete (end-to-end). For typical short requests (<=128 tokens) we guarantee 700 ms p95 on Dedicated; for longer outputs the latency scales and is a function of tokens produced — we model this with tokens/sec execution rate and turning that into expected total latency.
- Uptime (Dedicated): 99.95% SLA with credits for breaches.

Proposed POC exception: Redwood will provide Dedicated serving lanes for Acme POC and commit the streaming TTFT p95 <= 350 ms and sustained >= 1,200 tokens/sec for the model in the SOW. If we can’t meet the TTFT requirement during the POC cadence run, Redwood will: 1) open an engineering action to pre-warm KV cache, 2) enable a temporary smaller-context model fallback for burst traffic, and 3) provide one-time service credit equal to 10% of that month’s Dedicated fee if targets are missed more than twice.

Karthik — can you confirm these numbers from an infra perspective and update the draft SLA?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[attachment: streaming_sla_draft.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, Ethan Moore <ethan.moore@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-11T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming vs batch SLA — need specifics for POC

Ethan, Sean —

Digging into numbers from our runtime tests and the Dedicated instance classes we propose for the POC. A few clarifications and constraints to make the commitment actionable:

1) TTFT definition: time from request arrival at our edge to the first token byte emitted to the client. We measure at our edge (not at customer network). Network hop adds variable latency; recommend you measure on your side too.
2) Streaming TTFT commitments (Dedicated, p95):
   - Short responses (<=128 tokens): TTFT p95 <= 300 ms (we can tighten to 250 ms if Acme purchases pre-warming as part of POC).
   - Long responses (>=1024 tokens): TTFT p95 <= 450 ms.
3) Sustained generation rate (tokens/sec):
   - We guarantee >= 1,200 tokens/sec sustained per serving lane for the selected model family (quantized weights as specified).
   - For workloads that require >1,200 tokens/sec we recommend scaling out lanes; our autoscaler can provision additional lanes with a short warm-up (30–90s) if burst policy enabled.
4) Non-streaming endpoints (blocking):
   - We express these as end-to-end response completeness. Empirically for the chosen model class we observe generation rates ~600–900 tokens/sec per lane; for p95 latency guarantees we size lanes accordingly.
5) Failure modes & mitigations: cache cold-starts increase TTFT; token/sec drops if KV cache misses cascade. We will instrument and add alerts (tracing + profiling) during the POC so we can correlate misses.

Attached is the runtimes_latency_report.csv with recent test runs and a draft wording for the POC exception.

Acceptance wording we propose to insert into SOW: "Redwood will provision Dedicated serving lanes for the Acme POC and commits to a streaming endpoint TTFT p95 <= 350 ms for short outputs (<=128 tokens) and sustained token generation >= 1,200 tokens/sec per lane. In the event Redwood does not meet the TTFT or throughput targets during the POC validation window (two or more failing runs), Redwood will apply the mitigation steps described in the attached appendix and issue a one-time service credit as specified."

Let me know if you want the pre-warm add-on included as an explicit line item; that’s the quickest lever to get TTFT down to ~250 ms p95.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
[attachment: runtimes_latency_report.csv (CSV, 48KB)]

From: Ethan Moore <ethan.moore@acme.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-12T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming vs batch SLA — need specifics for POC

Team —

This is exactly what we needed. The proposed POC exception wording looks good; we’ll accept Dedicated lanes for the POC and add the pre-warm add-on to the SOW to target the tighter TTFT (250 ms p95). Also appreciate the mitigation steps and the one-time credit — that should be sufficient for procurement.

Next steps from our side: I’ll have Procurement send a redline of the SOW with the SLA appendix and we’ll aim to kick off the POC the week of Apr 26.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Moore
ENG Manager, Real-Time Systems
Acme Corp
